body:
A tenant representation brief explains what your business needs from its premises, when a decision is required and which costs and constraints matter. Before meeting a Newcastle tenant representative, gather your current lease dates, team and space requirements, location priorities and occupancy budget. You do not need every answer before starting; mark uncertain items so they can be resolved.

This guide is for Newcastle, Lake Macquarie and Hunter businesses considering a renewal, relocation or new commercial lease. It is a planning checklist, with no claims about past client savings or current market rents.

## Start with the deadline that can change your options

Record the lease expiry, any option notice dates, planned opening date and the earliest date you could realistically move. Include the dates exactly as written in the lease and ask your solicitor to confirm what the notice provisions require. Do not assume the expiry date is the only deadline that matters.

If your lease ends soon, say so at the first conversation. The search, negotiation, documentation, fit out and move all need to fit into the available time. If you are uncertain about a date, provide the relevant documents rather than guessing.

## Describe how the premises must work

Start with the people, activities and equipment the space needs to support. Include peak attendance rather than only total headcount, visitor numbers, meeting needs, storage, accessibility requirements and any specialist use. Separate essentials from preferences so an attractive listing does not silently change the brief.

For an office, consider focused work and meeting capacity alongside desks. For another commercial use, describe the actual activity and the specialist inputs needed to assess suitability. A floor area alone is not a complete property brief.

| Brief item | What to record | Question to resolve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Timing | Expiry, notice dates, opening and move targets | Which dates need solicitor confirmation? |
| Space | Peak attendance, activities, equipment and storage | What must the premises support on a busy day? |
| Location | Preferred suburbs and staff, customer or supplier travel needs | Which locations are essential and which are flexible? |
| Occupancy cost | Rent, outgoings and other recurring premises costs | Which costs are included in each option? |
| Setup | Fit out, furniture, moving and existing items to retain | What must be funded before occupation? |
| Authority | Decision maker and approval process | Who can approve terms, expenditure and appointments? |

## Use Newcastle locations as criteria, not assumptions

For a Newcastle CBD brief, record the staff and visitor access you need and check the particular building's loading, parking and delivery arrangements. For premises in Maryville, Wickham, Lake Macquarie or elsewhere in the Hunter, apply the same method to the actual site. A suburb name does not establish suitability, cost or building capability.

Choose a workable search area based on the business's requirements. If two locations could work, list the differences that would affect the decision rather than excluding one without a reason.

## Separate annual occupancy costs from moving costs

Bring the current rent and available outgoings information, and identify what else the business pays to occupy the premises. Record whether amounts include GST so comparisons use the same basis. Keep fit out, furniture, moving, professional fees and potential end-of-lease work visible as separate planning items.

The purpose is to give the tenant representative a clear commercial starting point. It does not replace legal, accounting or project-specific advice, and it is not a promise that every cost can be removed through negotiation.

[Read how to compare commercial leases](/blog/how-to-compare-commercial-leases)

## Bring the documents you already have

Useful documents include the signed lease and relevant amendments, current plans, outgoings statements if available, landlord correspondence, renewal proposals and any existing project brief. Tell the team which documents are missing and who can obtain them.

Before formal engagement, ask what the tenant representative will do, how fees and any relevant third-party arrangements work, what authority is required and what remains with your solicitor or other advisers. Agree the scope before work starts.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I speak to a tenant representative before choosing a property?

Yes. An early brief lets the search criteria and decision process be established before a listing creates pressure. Bring what you know and flag the gaps.

### Can a tenant representative help if I want to stay in my current premises?

Yes. A renewal brief can examine how the current premises serve the business, the proposed commercial terms and the practical alternatives. The appropriate approach depends on the lease and available time.

### Do I need to know the exact floor area?

No. Start with the activities, attendance, meeting, storage and equipment requirements. A usable space brief can then be tested against layouts and premises options.

### Does a tenant representative replace my solicitor?

No. YOS supports the tenant's commercial brief, options and negotiation workstream. Your appointed solicitor advises on legal terms and documentation.

### What if my budget or move date is uncertain?

Explain the uncertainty and identify who can resolve it. Record a working assumption rather than presenting it as an approved budget or fixed deadline.
